# Codemap — issue 0147, the two pinned evaluator gaps

Every file the issue has to change, one line each; the increment a file belongs to is named in its line, and a file without one is on both paths.

- `src/evaluator/infoProjection.js` — Collects the info elements of a slot; today an effectively hidden node contributes nothing at all, which is why the hidden unit's own profile occurrence is missing from the report (increment hidden-slot-info).
- `src/evaluator/report.js` — Emits `infoElements` per slot and derives an anchor's `current` from a constraint result's `actual` — the reporting end of both increments.
- `src/evaluator/infoProjection.test.js` — Unit test that pins today's rule that a hidden node's own projection stays empty and that nothing is inherited from it; the scenario contradicts the first half (increment hidden-slot-info).
- `src/evaluator/infoElements.test.js` — Unit test that pins base-hidden and modifier-hidden info elements end to end through `evaluate`; the neighbouring rule to the one the scenario moves (increment hidden-slot-info).
- `src/evaluator/modifiers.js` — Holds the `set-primary`/`unset-primary` category handlers and the handler registry that binds them to the category target (increment set-primary-membership).
- `src/evaluator/effectiveState.js` — Stores effective category membership, the primary flag and the per-(node, carrier) hidden flag that both the counting and the info projection read.
- `src/evaluator/countIndex.js` — Derives the targets a node is countable under from its effective categories; the path by which a modifier-granted membership reaches a category anchor (increment set-primary-membership).
- `src/evaluator/evalTree.js` — Synthesizes the force-level category anchors whose `current` the scenario pins, and yields the info carriers of a definition that the projection walks.
- `src/evaluator/constraints.js` — Computes the `actual` of a limit at each anchor — both the Regiment-of-Renown count and the firing `.gst` Rare limit come from here (increment set-primary-membership).
- `src/evaluator/fixpoint.js` — Fixes the order in which modifier effects reach a freshly built count index and the anchor post-pass; the rounds decide whether a modifier-granted membership is visible to the anchors (increment set-primary-membership).
- `src/evaluator/report.effectiveCategories.test.js` — Unit test that pins the current `set-primary`/`unset-primary` contract for membership and the primary flag (increment set-primary-membership).
- `src/evaluator/countIndex.syntheticAnchors.test.js` — Unit test that pins what the synthetic anchors count (increment set-primary-membership).

return.plan:
## What is wrong

`collectInfoElements` in `src/evaluator/infoProjection.js` opens with `if (effective.isHidden(node)) return;`, so a slot that is effectively hidden gets `infoElements: []` in its capability record. In `docs/testing/set-characteristic-force-gate/rosters/02-standard-force-mv-base-7.ros` the unit `Tomb stalker` (`f401a3ed-077e-4795-b32d-ee659bd0b37a`) keeps its base `hidden="true"` — its `set hidden=false` is gated on force `f37a-a93e-fa22-61a8`, which this roster does not use — so its own profile occurrence never reaches the report and the case fails on `infoElements: kein Info-Element mit id="fe84bf5a-..." am Slot.`

Nothing else stands in the way, verified against the fixture `src/evaluator/__fixtures__/whfb6-definitive/Vampire Counts (6th definitive edition).cat`:
- the carrier `infoLink fe84bf5a-d0f1-4b5e-ae5d-475128f4ee32` has `hidden="false"` and its target profile `d2b729f3-3d5d-4d5b-84a8-cb1906d4ba77` has `hidden="false"`, so the per-carrier gate `effective.isHidden(node, carrier)` lets it through;
- both modifiers on that link (`set value="6" field="0e92-d038-82bf-fb41"` and `set value="Tomb stalker" field="name"`) sit in a `modifierGroup` whose only condition is the force `instanceOf` gate, so with the gate off `effective.nameOf(node, carrier)` yields the link name "Tomb Scorpion" and `effective.characteristicEntriesOf` yields the base Mv 7 / WS 4 / Sv+ 5 the criterion asks for;
- `entryKindOf` maps the link to its target kind `profile`, and `buildProfileEntry` uses `carrier.id`, so the entry appears under `fe84bf5a-...`.

So one gate is the whole defect, and one file changes.

## The rule that replaces it

Effective hiddenness governs what a slot contributes to **another** slot, not what its **own** record carries. Concretely:

1. A slot's own record always carries its own effectively visible carriers, whether or not the slot itself is hidden.
2. A hidden node contributes nothing upward — neither its own carriers nor anything from its subtree — so an ancestor's record is unchanged by this increment.
3. The per-carrier gate is untouched: an element that is itself effectively hidden (base `hidden` or a `field="hidden"` modifier on the carrier) stays out everywhere.

Grounding: `docs/battlescribe-data-format.md` §8 defines `hidden` as "not shown to the user" and suppresses min-validation for a hidden entity; it makes no claim that a hidden entity loses its profiles. The report materializes hidden slots and marks them with `isHidden` instead of dropping them (ADR-0035, quoted in the header of `report.js`); emptying their info projection contradicts that materialization. The scenario, authored black-box from the catalog data under ADR-0033, is the specification and states rule 1 outright.

## The change (only `src/evaluator/infoProjection.js`)

Split the single recursion into two named functions so the rule reads off the code:

- `collectOwnInfoElements(node, context, entries)` — today's carrier loop verbatim: iterate `infoCarriersOf(node.def)`, `continue` on `effective.isHidden(node, carrier)`, build via `INFO_ENTRY_BUILDERS`, push non-`NO_ENTRY` entries.
- `collectInheritedInfoElements(node, context, entries)` — for each `child` of `node.children`: skip `child.isPhantom` (unchanged), skip when `effective.isHidden(child)` (this keeps the child's whole subtree out, exactly as today's early return did), otherwise call `collectOwnInfoElements(child, ...)` then `collectInheritedInfoElements(child, ...)`.
- `infoElementsOf(node, effective, registry)` calls own first, then inherited, preserving the documented order "own elements first, then those of the occupied sub-selections in tree order".

Rewrite the module header of `infoProjection.js`: the paragraph "── Was *nicht* enthalten ist ──" states the superseded rule and must state the new one instead — own record always, upward contribution gated by the node's effective visibility, carrier gate unchanged — naming the scenario `set-characteristic-force-gate` and format doc §8 as the reason. Keep the file's German prose style.

### Alternatives rejected

- **An `isProjectionRoot` boolean on the existing recursion.** Same behaviour in one line less, but the rule then lives inside a flag; two named collectors say it out loud. Rejected for readability, not correctness.
- **Dropping the node gate entirely (own and inherited).** A hidden sub-selection's rules would then surface on the visible parent's slot. That contradicts the still-valid unit case 'erbt nichts von einem versteckten Knoten' and the inheritance statements of `docs/testing/info-projection`, and the scenario at hand demands nothing of the kind. Rejected.
- **Special-casing the unit/`OCCUPIED` anchor kind.** The scenario speaks about a slot, not an anchor kind; a kind-specific rule would leave hidden offer anchors on the old rule and split one contract into two. Rejected.

## Consequences to expect

- Every hidden slot's capability now carries its own info elements — occupied hidden slots and hidden offer anchors alike. This cannot break the committed scenarios: `infoElements` in the manifest is a subset assertion, and the only `infoElementsAbsent` lists in the whole of `docs/testing/` sit in `docs/testing/info-projection/scenario.json` on slots that are not hidden, naming either a carrier that is itself hidden (`7f0b-...`, `bd66-...`, `b600-...`) or a parent's element that must not travel downward (`48e1-...`, `3f1c-...`) or an `infoGroup` identity (`fd0e-...`, `fb4b-...`). None of the three is touched.
- No other production module calls `infoElementsOf`; `report.js` only forwards it into `toCapability`. `report.js`, `effectiveState.js`, `evalTree.js` and `countIndex.js` need no edit for this increment.
- `src/components/**` reads `capability.infoElements` (`UnitChips.jsx`, `UnitSelectionCard.jsx`, `PlayUnitDetails.jsx`, `PlayMode.jsx`). Those files and their tests are outside the increment's boundary and outside the check command; do not touch them.

## Doc drift you must not fix here

`docs/evaluator-architecture.md` still states the superseded rule in §3.6 ("**Verstecktes bleibt draußen.** Ausgeschlossen ist, was **selbst** versteckt ist, und alles, was an einem **versteckten Knoten** hängt.", and again in the report-shape comment "und Regeltexte, Verstecktes ausgenommen"). Criterion 5 forbids changing any file outside `src/evaluator/`, so leave it untouched in this increment and let a later step correct it. Do not weaken the change to keep that sentence true.

- **C1 — re-pin the superseded case (replaces `laesst die eigene Projektion eines versteckten Knotens leer`, lines 250–254).** Input: the block's `CATALOGUE_XML` and `rosterWithOption({ withOption: true })`, i.e. the option `entry-option` is chosen and an unconditional `set field="hidden" value="true"` hides it. Do not delete the case and do not soften it to a `toContain`.
- **C2 — the carrier gate survives on a hidden node (edge).** Extend the block's `CATALOGUE_XML`: give the hidden option a second rule with `hidden="true"` (a new id constant, e.g. `rule-hidden-of-hidden-option`). Expected: `infoElementIdsOfSlot(report, OPTION_ID)` contains `OPTION_RULE_ID` and does not contain the new base-hidden id. This is the case that proves only the node gate moved. Adjust C1's `toEqual` list accordingly if you place the new rule in the same entry — keep C1 an exact-list assertion.
- **C3 — keep `erbt nichts von einem versteckten Knoten` (lines 243–248) exactly as it is.** It pins the surviving half of the rule: with the option hidden, `infoElementIdsOfSlot(report, UNIT_ID)` must not contain `OPTION_RULE_ID`. Turn the researcher's test plan into failing tests. You have never seen an
implementation, so your tests encode what was asked for and cannot inherit an
implementer's misreading.

## How you work

1. **Read your brief.** Read `issue.md` for the intent and the acceptance
   criteria; the test plan is the `testPlan` field of the researcher's step in
   the run state, and your prompt names the command that reads that step. It is
   everything you are told about the change: take no other field of it — the
   implementation plan is not yours, and reading it would put an implementer's
   design in front of the tests that are meant to be independent of one. Do no
   research of your own either: a test written against the code that exists
   tests the implementation instead of the intent, so you do not open production
   code at all.
2. **Write the planned cases.** The test plan is your work order — the cases,
   their level, the file each goes in, and the command that runs it. The
   conventions of that file — its helpers, its fixtures, where a case belongs,
   how cases are named — live in the suite doc, the `CLAUDE.md` in the test
   directory, which is in your context the moment you work there. Write the
   planned cases in that style. Add no coverage the plan did not ask for, drop
   none it listed, and leave anything it marked as deliberately untested
   untested. Decide the small things it left open yourself, in the suite's
   style.
3. **Test behaviour, not implementation.** If a case is too vague to pin to a
   concrete expected outcome, or contradicts the criterion it claims to cover,
   write what you can and put the conflict in `openQuestions`. A guessed
   expectation is worse than none, and rewriting the plan yourself is worse than
   both.
4. **Prove the failures.** Run your own tests with the single-file command the
   plan names, and confirm each fails because the behaviour is missing — not an
   import error, not a typo. Quote the failure in your return. The suite and
   the linter are not yours to run; the implementer runs what the plan lists
   once the code exists.
5. **Keep the suite doc current.** You are the one changing the suite, so the
   `CLAUDE.md` beside it is yours: where your tests change what it says — a
   new helper, a new section, a renamed convention — update it in the same
   commit as the tests. Where none exists, write one from the file you just
   worked in: what the suite covers, the helpers and fixtures a new case
   reuses, where a case belongs, how cases are named, what is faked and what
   is real, and the command that runs just this suite. Where the test plan
   reported the doc wrong, correcting it is yours too. Keep it lean — every
   line is context the next agent pays for.

In a correction round the criterion is a reviewer's reproduction spec instead of
the whole intent, and the test plan of that round's researcher step is written
for it. Write that case and nothing else. Earlier rounds are done with. The reviewer never writes
tests; you do.

## Boundaries

- Test files and the suite doc beside them only. Production code is off
  limits, even a one-line stub.
- You never make a test pass. The implementer does that, and may not edit what
  you wrote.

## What you record

Walk the test plan case by case. What you write into `backlog.json` is the whole
of what the implementer gets about the tests — it reads your step, and no prompt
carries any of this. Its fields:

- **`cases`** — one entry per planned case: the case in the plan's words, the
  test file by path, the test's name, what the case demands, and the failure it
  produced. For a case you did not write, leave `file` and `testName` empty and
  say in `got` why.
- **`openQuestions`** — every gap and conflict you found in the test plan, one
  line each. The next research round picks them up; they do not stop the run.
- **`questions`** — what the shared brief defines it as. A vague test case is
  not one of those: it goes in `openQuestions`.

Your prompt names every field this step returns, `summary` among them. Record
the return into `backlog.json` under the label your prompt names, the way the
shared brief describes: the cases live in that file alone.

return.summary: Issue 0147 is cut into two increments, one per acceptance criterion: `hidden-slot-info` makes a hidden unit slot report its own profile occurrence (criterion 1, scenario set-characteristic-force-gate), and `set-primary-membership` makes an unconditional `set-primary field="category"` secure category membership on its own without removing any (criterion 2, scenario set-primary-category-membership). The codemap in backlog.json names twelve files across `src/evaluator/`, the two pinned gaps kept apart.

cut.why-two: The two acceptance criteria are two unrelated paths through the engine: the first is the info projection of a slot, the second is the way a modifier-granted category membership reaches an anchor's count. Neither decision constrains the other, each is separately reviewable, and each leaves the suite green on its own. Merging them into one increment would put two independent root causes into one review; splitting either further would produce halves that only make sense together (a projection change nobody reads, a membership change nothing counts).
cut.why-this-order: `hidden-slot-info` first because it is the load-bearing one: `src/evaluator/infoProjection.js` drops every info element of an effectively hidden node, and a unit test (`infoProjection.test.js`, 'laesst die eigene Projektion eines versteckten Knotens leer') pins exactly the rule the scenario contradicts. Moving that contract can ripple through every slot in the report, so the run learns its cost in the first increment rather than the last. `set-primary-membership` is independent and cannot be blocked by it.
cut.criteria-mapping: Acceptance criterion 1 (docs/testing/set-characteristic-force-gate, failing roster 02) lands wholly in `hidden-slot-info`. Acceptance criterion 2 (docs/testing/set-primary-category-membership, failing rosters 01 and 03) lands wholly in `set-primary-membership`, including the second half of that criterion — the Rare anchor reaching 2 and the `.gst` limit `0a44-2d3f-adfe-f3a1` firing with actual 2 / bound 1 — because it is the same membership rule seen from the other side and would be untestable apart from it. No criterion is in two increments and none is unassigned.
cut.rejected: Rejected a cut by engine layer (modifier application, then counting, then reporting): every slice would leave the repository half-migrated and none would make a scenario green. Rejected a separate increment for the firing Rare limit of roster 03: it is the same code change as roster 01's anchor count, and pinning it apart would build the same fix twice.

open-code-facts.hidden-slot-info: The cause is located and needs no further planning: `src/evaluator/infoProjection.js` returns early for an effectively hidden node, so the hidden Tomb stalker slot projects nothing at all. What the new rule should be — a hidden node's own carriers project, its children still do not inherit upward, or something narrower — is the researcher's to settle against `docs/battlescribe-data-format.md` and the scenario.
open-code-facts.set-primary-membership: The cause is not located, deliberately. The obvious handlers already look right: `modifiers.js` binds `set-primary` on a category target to `effectiveState.setPrimaryCategory`, which adds the membership before setting the flag, and `countIndex.targetsOf` counts a node under its effective categories. The anchor's `current` is not a count of its own but a constraint result's `actual` (`report.js`, `current: maxResult?.actual ?? minResult?.actual ?? 0`), so the miss may sit anywhere on the path modifier -> effective state -> count index -> constraint at the synthesized force-level category anchor, including the fixpoint round order (`fixpoint.js`) that decides when a modifier effect is visible to a freshly built index. The increment is cut so that the researcher answers this first; it is a code fact, not a human decision.

return.scope-notes: The issue's out-of-scope section settles two things that would otherwise be questions: no file under `docs/testing/` may change (the scenarios are the specification, including `campaign-state.json`'s pinned gaps), and nothing outside `src/evaluator/` and its unit tests may change. Both are written into every increment's criteria. The check command is `npx vitest run src/evaluator` for both increments, per the issue's Decisions.
